StackType.issue: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30 against today's tree (power/_stack_type_single, shared with burrowed/hellraiser/etc. -- power-1/3/5 sites, not re-derived here). PowerStackType.Single, and this is the one unit in the on_stack family that goes the OTHER way: the sim does NOT override on_stack (`'on_stack' in IllusionPower.__dict__` is False, executed), so a second application adds via the base `Power.on_stack`. That happens to be what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236), so it is *more* faithful than the 15 units that override it to `pass` -- but it is still a gap, because C#'s AfterApplied fires only on a genuinely new power while the sim's __init__-time Minion grant (powers.py:1887-1889 `if "minion" not in owner.powers: PowerCmd.apply(hooks, owner, MinionPower, 1)`) likewise only runs on construction (`Power.__init__`), never on `on_stack` -- so a second Illusion application still cannot re-fire the Minion grant. DORMANT, enumerated: (1) nothing reads Illusion's `.amount` anywhere in the class body (powers.py:1859-1917, read in full: is_reviving, should_power_be_removed_on_death, should_remove_from_combat_after_death, on_death, should_allow_hitting, revive -- none touch self.amount) or in either ported applier (monsters/hive/the_obscura.py, monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py); (2) the sim's stacking path (cmds.py:567-580, `if power_cls.id in target.powers: existing.on_stack(amount)`) calls `on_stack` on the EXISTING instance and never re-runs `__init__`, so a second application cannot re-trigger the Minion grant through this path either, matching C#'s AfterApplied-only-fires-once shape by construction rather than by the StackType. Both ported appliers (Parafright, EyeWithTeeth) apply IllusionPower exactly once in `__init__` with no second application site anywhere in the sim. Named trigger: any second IllusionPower application to an owner (a second summon of the same creature instance, which no ported content does), or a caller reading `.amount`. Recorded so the inconsistency between this unit and its 15 `on_stack->pass` siblings stays visible.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath.issue: Closed 2026-07-29 (round 7): STALE, not open, and by rule 3 with the seam entry it shares a mechanism with (creature_card_cmds/step8b, closed earlier this round on the same evidence). The entry says the hook is unreachable "because an Illusion's own death takes the PREVENTION arm (powers.py `should_die` -> False)". IllusionPower HAS NO `should_die` OVERRIDE -- `'should_die' in IllusionPower.__dict__` is False, executed today. It implements `should_remove_from_combat_after_death` (IllusionPower.cs:108-114) and nothing else on the death side, so the killed creature takes the REAL arm, which is the arm that calls `_strip_powers_after_death`. EXECUTED 2026-07-29 on a real Parafright (encounter [TheObscura, Parafright]) given a player-applied Vulnerable 3 and killed: powers go ['illusion', 'minion', 'vulnerable'] -> ['illusion', 'minion'] with the corpse still in `enemies` and `is_dead` True. That is IllusionPower.cs:59-66 exactly -- the non-temporary Debuff IS stripped, the two Buffs are kept. The `is_temporary` stand-in for the absent ITemporaryPower marker is unchanged and remains the one approximation here. NOT CLOSED: nothing -- this entry carried no residue beyond the marker note.  The text it replaced read: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE HOOK NOW EXISTS AND THIS POWER IMPLEMENTS IT: `hooks.should_power_be_removed_on_death` is consulted by `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py:67-83, called from the real-death arm at cmds.py:50), and `IllusionPower.should_power_be_removed_on_death` (powers.py:1647-1656) reproduces IllusionPower.cs:59-66 -- keep buffs, drop non-temporary debuffs -- with `getattr(power, 'is_temporary', False)` standing in for the still-absent ITemporaryPower marker. WHAT REMAINS is that it is unreachable for the case it was written for: an Illusion's own death takes the PREVENTION arm (powers.py:1671 `should_die` -> False), which never calls `_strip_powers_after_death`. So the LIVE debuff half is unchanged -- an Eye with Teeth given Vulnerable 3 and killed still revives holding it. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py:30-83 and powers.py.

AfterApplied.rationale: C# grants MinionPower 1 from AfterApplied unless the owner already has it (IllusionPower.cs:68-75, applier null, cardSource null); the sim does it in __init__ with the same `"minion" not in owner.powers` test (powers.py:1562-1564) and the same absent applier. The sim has no AfterApplied slot, and __init__ runs at exactly the point PowerCmd.apply creates the power (cmds.py:324-327) -- i.e. BEFORE hooks.on_power_applied rather than after, which is the only difference and is unobservable because no ported listener reacts to a Minion grant. Named per the main report's section 7 item 6: the mechanism is __init__-for-AfterApplied, and it would break for any AfterApplied body that needs the power to already be registered.

AfterDeath.maps_to: powers.py:1900-1911 IllusionPower.on_death + should_allow_hitting + revive(), fired from the DEATH (real) arm of cmds._resolve_death (cmds.py:102-136)
AfterDeath.rationale: STALE as filed. RE-EXECUTED 2026-07-30: the record's premise ('powers.py:1671-1675 still implements this via should_die returning False, so the sim takes the prevention arm') no longer matches the source. The live IllusionPower class (powers.py:1859-1917) has NO `should_die` override at all -- EXECUTED: `grep -rn "def should_die\\b" sts2_rl/` returns exactly 2 hits, hooks.py:1196 (the dispatcher) and potions.py:1337 (Fairy in a Bottle); zero in powers.py -- matching IllusionPower.cs, which has no ShouldDie override either (read in full: Type, StackType, ShouldPlayVfx, FollowUpStateId, ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath, AfterApplied, AfterDeath, ShouldAllowHitting, ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath, AfterCombatEnd, ReviveMove). So a Parafright/Eye-with-Teeth kill runs `_resolve_death`'s DEATH arm (cmds.py:113-122) -- the REAL-death arm in C# too (CreatureCmd.cs:505-537) -- and `hooks.on_death(target, False)` fires (cmds.py:121), so `IllusionPower.on_death`'s `if was_removal_prevented or creature is not self.owner: return` (powers.py:1904-1906) sees `was_removal_prevented=False`, mirroring C#'s `if (!wasRemovalPrevented && creature == base.Owner)` (IllusionPower.cs:76-77) exactly, and both arm the revive flag (`is_reviving`/`isReviving`) unconditionally once that guard passes. `_strip_powers_after_death` (cmds.py:139-155) is no longer skipped -- it is the death arm's own unconditional tail (cmds.py:122) -- and it consults `hooks.should_power_be_removed_on_death`, so the buff-keep/non-temp-debuff-drop split (already separately verdicted faithful on this record's `ShouldPowerBeRemovedOnDeath` hook) actually runs. THE REVIVE_MOVE SPLICE: C#'s `SetMoveImmediate(REVIVE_MOVE)` forces the very next turn to be the heal turn, overriding whatever the machine would otherwise have done; the sim reproduces the same observable without a state-machine splice because neither ported applier is a `MachineMonster` -- `Parafright.take_turn`/`EyeWithTeeth.take_turn` (monsters/hive/the_obscura.py:54-58, monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py:48-52) check `illusion.is_reviving` FIRST, before any normal-move logic, and `current_intent` does the same, so the flag flip inside `on_death` (executed synchronously, before the caller returns) is visible immediately and forces the heal turn exactly as `SetMoveImmediate` does. `ShouldAllowHitting` (powers.py:1908-1911) matches IllusionPower.cs:96-104 (`creature != base.Owner -> true; else !IsReviving`) line for line, so the reviving owner is untargetable in both engines. `revive()` (powers.py:1913-1917) reproduces `ReviveMove`'s `Heal(MaxHp - CurrentHp)` (IllusionPower.cs:127); the two remaining ReviveMove statements (`TriggerAnim WakeUpTrigger`, the Parafright SFX) are presentation, already separately waived on this record. EXECUTED AND PINNED: test/test_hive.py::TestTheObscura::test_parafright_revives_instead_of_dying -- kills a live Parafright with 999 damage, asserts `illusion.is_reviving`, `current_intent.move_type == HEAL`, unhittable (`DamageCmd.deal(...) == 0`), and after `end_turn()` the creature is at full HP with `is_reviving` cleared. SECOND EXECUTED WITNESS (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/power-2-illusion-death.py`): an EyeWithTeeth given non-temporary Vulnerable(2) and killed with 999 damage ends `is_dead=True, hp=0, retained_after_death=True`, powers `['illusion','minion','vulnerable']` -> `['illusion','minion']` (the debuff stripped, the buffs kept, matching `should_power_be_removed_on_death`), `is_reviving=True`. VERIFIED by reading powers.py:1859-1917, cmds.py:102-155, monsters/hive/the_obscura.py and monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py in full, and src/Core/Models/Powers/IllusionPower.cs in full.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.maps_to: powers.py:1891-1898 IllusionPower.should_remove_from_combat_after_death, consulted at cmds.py:118-120 on the death arm
ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.rationale: STALE as filed. Settled independently of the AfterDeath entry above by executing this witness itself, not by inheriting its label: the premise ('this power still does not implement should_remove_from_combat_after_death, because it reaches retention through should_die instead') is false. `IllusionPower.should_remove_from_combat_after_death` (powers.py:1891-1898) reads `return creature is not self.owner`, which is `ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` (IllusionPower.cs:106-113: `if (creature != base.Owner) return true; return false;`) read line for line, and the power's own comment now says so explicitly: 'This is the ONLY death-side predicate the power implements -- it has no ShouldDie override at all, so the death is REAL and only the removal is refused.' It is genuinely consulted: `_resolve_death`'s death arm sets `target.retained_after_death = not hooks.should_remove_from_combat_after_death(target)` (cmds.py:118-120), the sim's port of `Hook.ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath` gating `shouldRemoveFromCombat` at CreatureCmd.cs:507. So the reviving creature IS retained via this hook, not via an unconditional prevention-arm flag as the stale text claimed -- the prevention arm is not even reached (see the AfterDeath entry and guard g6). VERIFIED by reading powers.py:1859-1917 and cmds.py:102-136 together.

guards.issue: RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30, survives the AfterDeath fix (now faithful, see above): a public settable property with no sim analogue at all, letting an applier choose which state the revived creature resumes on (default: the last LOGGED state). The sim's revive reproduces C#'s forced-next-turn-heal observable through a boolean flag (`is_reviving`, checked first in `take_turn`/`current_intent`) rather than a state-machine splice, so there is no notion of "which state to resume on" to diverge over. DORMANT, enumerated: neither ported applier is even a `MachineMonster` any more -- `Parafright` and `EyeWithTeeth` (monsters/hive/the_obscura.py, monsters/overgrowth/fogmog.py) are plain `Monster` subclasses with ONE hard-coded non-reviving move each (SLAM, DISTRACT respectively) and no move-state graph, so there is no second state to resume to and the flag-check shape is observationally identical to always resuming the single move. Named trigger unchanged: an IllusionPower applier with more than one move state (none ported), or a caller that sets the C# property (none exists in the sim).

guards.what: The prevention branch's HP contract: sim `hp = 1` vs C# leaving the creature at 0 and re-entering KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition
guards.issue: NARROWED 2026-07-27. THE FLOOR IS GONE: `_resolve_death`'s prevention (else) arm (cmds.py:123-136) no longer writes `target.hp = 1`; it leaves the creature dead at 0 HP, sets `retained_after_death = True`, fires `on_death(..., True)` and then `after_preventing_death` -- CreatureCmd.cs:560-571's shape. WHAT REMAINS is C#'s RE-ENTRY: CreatureCmd.cs:562-565 re-enters `KillWithoutCheckingWinCondition(creature, force, recursion + 1)` while `creature.IsDead`, up to 10 times before throwing `InvalidOperationException`; `_resolve_death`'s else-arm (cmds.py:123-136) simply returns with no re-check and no recursion cap. RE-VERDICTED DORMANT 2026-07-30, sharper than before: mechanism `power/_death_prevention_branch` is NOT reached via power/illusion at all any more -- IllusionPower has no `should_die` override (`grep -rn "def should_die\b" sts2_rl/` finds it nowhere in powers.py; see the AfterDeath entry above), so a Parafright/Eye-with-Teeth kill never enters this else-arm through Illusion. The branch is reached only through the sim's two ported `should_die`-family listeners, enumerated: (1) Fairy in a Bottle (potions.py:1337 `should_die`, `after_preventing_death` at :1340 heals `max(MaxHp * 0.30, 1)` -- always > 0), and (2) Lizard Tail (relics/lizard_tail.py:32 `should_die_late`, dispatched through the same `hooks.should_die(` call -- exactly one caller, `cmds._resolve_death` -- `after_preventing_death` heals 50% of Max HP, also always > 0). Both unconditionally heal the creature back above 0 before `_resolve_death` returns, so `creature.IsDead` is always False by the time C# would check whether to recurse -- the recursion/re-entry path this entry describes has no reachable trigger among ported content: no preventer that heals nothing, and no power (Illusion included) that reaches the else-arm without a preventer already having healed. VERIFIED by reading cmds.py:102-155, potions.py:1300-1345 and relics/lizard_tail.py in full. HANDOFF: mechanism `power/_death_prevention_branch` is shared with power-3/power-4's own sites (`power/adaptable/g5`, `power/steam_eruption/g4`); this finding is scoped to power/illusion's site only (Illusion does not reach the branch) and does not by itself settle the mechanism's liveness elsewhere -- see report HANDOFF section. Independently corroborated: `audit/records/power/adaptable.json`'s matching guard reached the identical conclusion (same two enumerated reachers, same date) for Adaptable's own site.
